premises.text: FluidDB is a shared database where any application can add any information to anything
premises.evidence_span: someone could build a shared database for applications where any application could come along and add any information to anything

premises.text: Independent related apps storing into FluidDB make unanticipated cross-app queries trivial
premises.evidence_span: I've combined data in an unanticipated way from three independent but related applications. And those applications are not aware of each other

premises.text: Apps can store information alongside related data without asking permission
premises.evidence_span: none of them had to ask permission to put that information into FluidDB

premises.text: FluidDB provides a shared writable object for everything as a platform for the web of things
premises.evidence_span: FluidDB gives you a shared, writable object for everything. In other words, it's a platform for the web of things

value.text: Related information becomes more valuable and useful when stored in one shared writable place
value.evidence_span: they're choosing to store their information into a place that makes it more valuable, because it's more useful

secondary_value.text: Writable social future of data not controlled solely by applications
secondary_value.evidence_span: The future of data is a writable future. It's one in which any person or any application can come along and add information to anything without asking for permission

causal_links.evidence_span: store their information into a place that makes it more valuable, because it's more useful

notes: Single coherent platform theory — one domain. Demo apps (Tickery/TunkRank/We Met At) treated as illustrations of one shared-store mechanism (§4.1.2), not separate premises. Funding anecdote excluded.
